title: MacWhisper vs Willow Voice on Mac in 2026: prices, privacy and which one to pick
metaTitle: MacWhisper vs Willow Voice on Mac: prices and privacy in 2026
description: MacWhisper vs Willow Voice on Mac: a one-time €64 license with optional local processing, or Willow's free plan and cloud dictation. Compare prices and privacy.
secondaryKeywords: macwhisper vs willow voice on mac
intro: MacWhisper is the better pick if you transcribe audio files and meetings on a Mac and want a one-time price. Willow Voice is the better pick if you dictate into many apps and also need Windows or an iPhone. Both dictate, but they charge and handle your data differently.
tldr: MacWhisper: a one-time €64 license on the vendor homepage, strongest for files, meetings and media on a Mac.
Willow Voice: a free plan, and PRO at $15 $12 per user per month with a Save 20% toggle. Works on Mac, Windows and iPhone.
Privacy: MacWhisper can keep sensitive audio on your Mac. Willow's default Private Mode does not keep dictated text or screen content, but dictation runs in the cloud.
Lazur is a third option: a voice assistant that points at things on screen and answers out loud, not a file transcriber.

blocks.text: MacWhisper vs Willow Voice at a glance

These two apps overlap on one job. Both turn your speech into text on a Mac. After that they split. MacWhisper leads with files, meetings and media, and lists dictation as one feature among several. Willow Voice is built around dictation into the app you are typing in. If most of your day is typing, Willow reads like the closer fit. If most of your day is audio you already have, MacWhisper usually fits better.
Treat the numbers above as a starting point, not a verdict. Price, platforms and privacy each change the answer. The sections below take them one at a time, with the caveats the sources give you.
MacWhisper vs Willow Voice price: one-time license or monthly seat

MacWhisper's vendor homepage lists Pro at €64 as a one-time license, with lifetime updates included. The free plan is €0 and free forever. Willow Voice lists PRO at $15 $12 per user per month, with a Monthly and Annual toggle that says Save 20%. Business is $35 $28 per month. Enterprise is custom.

Two caveats matter. The Gumroad listing for MacWhisper returned only its title when I checked, so its price there is unconfirmed. Check the Gumroad page before you buy there. Also, a review by Dave Swift lists the price as 59 euros, which does not match the vendor's €64. Trust the vendor page, and recheck it on the day you buy.

Price math depends on time. A license is paid once. A PRO seat is paid every month, or every year on annual billing. If you plan to use the app for years, a one-time price is easier to predict. If you want to test a workflow first, a free plan or a short paid stint costs less to start.

Read Willow's free tier closely. Dictation on the free plan uses a limited, weaker model. Scribe is capped at 20 uses per week. One Product Hunt reviewer says the free tier allows 2,000 words a week. The pricing page does not state that limit, so treat the reviewer's figure as unconfirmed.
MacWhisper vs Willow Voice on Windows and iPhone

MacWhisper is a Mac app. Its homepage mentions an iOS and iPad version in the FAQ. The release-notes mirror lists 15.10 as the latest version. Version 15.0 needs macOS 15 or later, and 13.24 was the last version that supported macOS 14. The mirror is not clearly the vendor's domain, so confirm the requirement on macwhisper.com.

Willow Voice lists Mac, Windows and iPhone on its homepage. If you split work between a Mac and a Windows PC, that alone can settle it. The only Android mention I found is a Product Hunt reviewer asking for an Android app. Neither product lists Android in the pages I checked.
Transcribing files, recordings and meetings with MacWhisper

This is where MacWhisper pulls ahead. Per its homepage, it transcribes uploaded files, microphone recordings and media URLs, including YouTube. It supports about 100 languages. It exports subtitle, text and document formats. Batch processing and speaker recognition are on the list too.

Meeting recording is the other big feature. MacWhisper describes recording in Zoom, Teams and Webex, with automatic start and end detection. It also offers watched folders and a command line tool. Dave Swift says speaker diarization is still in beta, so test it on a real recording before you trust the labels.

Take a common case. You have a recorded interview and need a quote from the middle of it. With MacWhisper, you add the file, run the transcription and search the text. In Willow, you would have to play the audio aloud and dictate over it, which is a different job.

Willow's pricing page, homepage and privacy policy describe dictation, Scribe and writing style memory. I did not find file transcription or meeting recording in its listed features. If you need those, ask Willow support before you pay, or pick MacWhisper.
Dictation accuracy and speed in MacWhisper and Willow Voice

Both apps let you dictate into text fields across the Mac. MacWhisper lists system-wide dictation. Willow lists use in any text field, more than 100 languages, a whisper mode and an offline mode on its homepage. Willow's help article does not mention offline mode, so test it with Wi-Fi off before you count on it.

Accuracy is where the reviews agree. Dave Swift says MacWhisper's dictation accuracy is noticeably better than Apple's native dictation. He also says basic dictation transcribes literally, so it does not tidy up what you say. Willow's reviewers mostly praise accuracy and speed. Those are opinions from small groups, so run your own test.

Speed is easier to measure. A 2016 lab study by Ruan and colleagues found speech input was 2.93 times faster than the keyboard for English short messages on touchscreen phones. Speech also made fewer errors, 5.30% against 11.22%. That study tested phones, not Macs, and it is old. It still explains why people switch from typing to talking.
Privacy: where MacWhisper and Willow Voice send your audio

MacWhisper's homepage says sensitive content can be processed locally, without data ever leaving your Mac. Cloud models and third-party AI services are optional. The page does not explain how those services handle data. Read that provider's policy before you turn on a cloud feature with private audio.

Willow processes dictation in the cloud, and its privacy policy says so. Private Mode is the default. In that mode, Willow does not retain dictated text or screen content, and audio is not used for model training. Dictation history stays on your device for viewing. If you opt in to Help Improve Willow, the company may keep anonymized recognized text, but not audio.

Willow's help article says no audio is stored on its servers. Audio stays on the device only for re-transcription. The homepage also claims SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA compliance and end-to-end encryption. Those are the company's own claims, so treat them as marketing until you read the audit or the contract.
The short version is simple. If your audio must not leave the Mac, MacWhisper's local path is the clearer story. Willow's Private Mode is strong on retention. Its dictation still runs in the cloud.
Where Lazur fits if you want a voice assistant, not a transcriber

Lazur is the third option here, and it works differently. It is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots come with it. Dictation is not the headline feature.

Lazur's product facts do not list file transcription or meeting recording. For a text file from a recording, pick MacWhisper. For a helper that explains the app in front of you, Lazur is built for that job.

Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both. The 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app, with no credit card. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available.
Mistakes people make when they choose between these apps

items: Buying Willow for file transcription. Its listed features focus on dictation, so check the feature list first.
Assuming MacWhisper's €64 covers every AI feature. AI prompts run on your own API keys, so you pay the AI provider on top of the license.
Reading Willow's free tier as unlimited. Scribe is capped at 20 uses per week on the free plan.
Believing Private Mode means nothing is stored. Dictation history stays on the device, and dictation still runs in the cloud.
Skipping the macOS check. MacWhisper 15.0 needs macOS 15 or later. A Mac on macOS 14 is limited to version 13.24.
Testing with one clean sample. Use your own accent, your jargon and the apps you really type in.

blocks.text: Edge cases to check before you buy

A few cases change the answer. If you use Windows at work, Willow is the only one of these two that lists Windows. If you work across an iPhone and a Mac, both products have an iPhone or iOS angle, so check which one you actually need. Both list around 100 languages, so test your own mix.

If you need on-screen help instead of transcription, the facts I checked for MacWhisper and Willow do not describe that. Lazur is built for it. For compliance, Willow's pricing page places enforced zero data retention, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA in its Business tier. Its help article lists enforced zero data retention under Enterprise. Ask Willow which plan you would get.
A one-week test to pick the right app

items: Pick one real job, such as a recorded call, a voice note or a draft email.
Check the price on the vendor pages on the day you test. Use macwhisper.com for MacWhisper and willowvoice.com/pricing for Willow.
Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone and confirm the app you test has access.
Time the job in each app. Count the corrections you make afterward.
Read the privacy policy for the mode you will actually use. For Willow, that is Private Mode by default.
Keep the app that needed fewer corrections, unless its price or privacy rules it out.

faq.question: Is MacWhisper cheaper than Willow Voice?
faq.answer: It depends on how long you use it. MacWhisper's vendor homepage lists a one-time €64 license. Willow's PRO plan shows $15 and $12 side by side, with a Save 20% label on its billing toggle. Check both pricing pages on the day you buy, because the Gumroad listing was not confirmed.

faq.question: Does Willow Voice work on Windows?
faq.answer: Yes, according to its homepage, which lists Mac, Windows and iPhone. MacWhisper's research notes list the Mac, with an iOS and iPad version mentioned in its FAQ. If you need Windows, check Willow first.

faq.question: Does MacWhisper send my audio to the cloud?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. MacWhisper says sensitive content can be processed locally, without data leaving your Mac. Cloud models and third-party AI services are optional. Read the provider's policy before you turn on a cloud feature.

faq.question: Is Willow Voice private?
faq.answer: Its default Private Mode says Willow does not retain dictated text or screen content. Dictation still runs in the cloud, and dictation history is stored on your device. The SOC 2 and HIPAA claims are the company's own, so read the audit or contract before you rely on them.

faq.question: Can Lazur transcribe audio files like MacWhisper?
faq.answer: Not from the product facts behind this page. Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen and answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate text at the cursor. For file transcription, MacWhisper is the better fit.

faq.question: What macOS do I need for MacWhisper?
faq.answer: The release-notes mirror says MacWhisper 15.0 requires macOS 15 or later. The latest version it lists is 15.10. A Mac on macOS 14 is limited to version 13.24. The mirror is not clearly the vendor's site, so confirm on macwhisper.com.

faq.question: Which one is more accurate for dictation?
faq.answer: Reviews differ in detail, not direction. Dave Swift says MacWhisper beats Apple's native dictation for accuracy, but its basic dictation transcribes literally. Willow's reviewers praise accuracy and speed. Test both on your own voice before you pay.

verdict: Pick MacWhisper if you transcribe audio files, meetings or YouTube links on a Mac and want a one-time license with local processing. Pick Willow Voice if you dictate into many apps, want a free plan to start, or need Windows or an iPhone too. Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that points at things on screen and answers out loud, not a transcriber.
